goal: Implement the first complete persistent-supervision vertical increment around the existing CGKN Telegram service: process health, identity-bound checkpoints, one resumable Codex thread, bounded result application, and an opt-in Provider-start gate.
acceptance_criteria: The supervisor host can start or attach to the existing Telegram bridge and records process identity plus fresh heartbeat state without persisting the Telegram token.
Checkpoint events have deterministic sequence, previous hash, self hash, repository identity, bounded context references, requested action, and fixed no-authority fields.
Two sequential checkpoints use the same stored Codex thread id; a restarted host resumes only from a coherent hash-bound cursor.

Strict result validation accepts only observe, advise, repair_cgkn, request_user_decision, resume, or halt and rejects candidate, evidence, package, delivery, secret, absolute-path, and traversal scope.

Telegram bridge startup plus Provider-before, Provider-validated, and failure points emit through the dedicated protocol; gate mode blocks Provider start until a matching resume/observe result exists.
The existing Provider validation, post-build finalization, local_packager, public_delivery_gate, delivery_manifest, whiteboard, and agent_session route remains unchanged.
Focused tests and a real read-only Codex start/resume smoke pass, while production daemon reliability and automatic repair remain honestly bounded by observed evidence.

quality_metrics.target: two or more separate checkpoints advance one cursor using the same stored thread id with no hash discontinuity
quality_metrics.method: mocked adapter integration test plus real read-only Codex smoke

quality_metrics.target: all authority-expanding actions and unsafe repair targets are rejected before application
host records a real child process identity and fresh bridge heartbeat without treating the Codex window or artifact presence as readiness
quality_metrics.method: mock child process tests and bounded local runtime smoke

quality_metrics.target: all existing kernel and Telegram route guards pass and no second generation or delivery call is introduced

prevention: Keep protocol, host, and Telegram intake integration in separate modules with explicit opt-in configuration.
assurance: Review all persisted fields for secrets and workflow-versus-evidence separation.
Review the bridge diff against the formal Provider and delivery route.
control: Run static compilation, protocol unit tests, host integration tests, Telegram/kernel regression, a real read-only Codex start/resume smoke, and full pytest.
improvement: Defer automatic code repair execution until the persistent audit and gate path is proven; retain repair_cgkn as a validated action requiring a separate governed executor.

interface_expectations: emit_checkpoint(state_dir, checkpoint_type, ...) appends one validated hash-linked event and returns its identity.
CodexCliThreadAdapter.run(checkpoint, thread_id) starts a persisted read-only thread when empty and resumes exactly that thread otherwise.
SupervisorHost.process_next() validates one event and result, persists the same thread id and cursor, and writes a result receipt.
await_checkpoint_release(state_dir, checkpoint_id, timeout) returns only a matching validated release decision.
telegram_live_bridge remains CGKN intake and the only default path into the reviewed Provider generation handoff.

feedback: The persistent host, same-thread Codex resume, hash-bound checkpoints, live Telegram heartbeat, bounded authority, and Provider-start gate passed offline and real runtime verification. The automatic repair executor remains deliberately deferred, so this increment is accepted with limits.

worked: A small vertical increment exposed the real process, encoding, import-path, thread-resume, and authority boundaries before adding automatic mutation.
Using a strict protocol separate from Telegram intake preserved the reviewed Provider and local_packager mainline.
did_not_work: The first Windows smoke used locale decoding for Codex JSONL, and the first detached launch used both an unreliable os.kill liveness probe and a file-path entrypoint that omitted the repository import root. Real startup evidence exposed and corrected all three defects.
experiments: Implement a separate governed repair executor that consumes validated repair_cgkn requests, records an auditable CGKN-only diff, runs proportional regression, and emits an explicit resume or rollback receipt.
